question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Perseverance
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Irresolution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Perseverance" means steady persistence in a course of action, especially despite difficulties or obstacles; continued effort to achieve something. (दृढ़ता, लगन)
◦ Example: Her perseverance during years of training finally earned her a place in the Olympic team.

• The antonym "Irresolution" means lack of firmness of purpose; hesitation or indecision, i.e., the opposite quality of steady determination. (अनिश्चय, दृढ़ता की कमी)
◦ Example: His irresolution made him abandon the project halfway.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Obstinacy (हठ): Stubborn adherence to one's own opinion or course, even when it may be unreasonable — this is not an antonym of perseverance but rather a related (if negative) form of persistence.

• Option 3: Readiness (तत्परता): The state of being fully prepared or willing to do something at once; it does not express the absence of persistence.

• Option 4: Eloquence (वाक्पटुता): Fluent and persuasive speaking or writing ability; unrelated in meaning to perseverance or its opposite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "Perseverance": Persistence, Tenacity, Diligence, Doggedness, Steadfastness.

• Other antonym pairs frequently asked by SSC: Diligence × Indolence, Tenacity × Vacillation, Steadfastness × Fickleness.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A group of worshippers
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Congregation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Congregation" means a group of people, especially worshippers, gathered together for religious observance or assembly. (उपासकों/श्रद्धालुओं का समूह)
◦ Example: The priest addressed the congregation at the end of the Sunday service.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Crowd (भीड़): A large, unorganised gathering of people in general, with no religious or specific connotation.

• Option 3: Caravan (काफिला): A group of people, especially traders or travellers, journeying together, typically through a desert.

• Option 4: Constellation (नक्षत्रमंडल): A group of stars forming a recognisable pattern in the sky; used figuratively also for a group of brilliant/famous people, but never for worshippers.

NOTE

• Other commonly asked one-word substitutions for groups: Flock (of birds/sheep), Herd (of cattle/elephants), Swarm (of bees/insects), Fleet (of ships), Choir (a group of singers, often in a church).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
He will return in a hour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. in a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Use of "a" and "an": The article "an" is used before words beginning with a vowel sound, not necessarily a vowel letter, while "a" is used before words beginning with a consonant sound.

• The word "hour" begins with a silent "h", so it is pronounced starting with the vowel sound /aʊ/. Hence it must be preceded by "an", not "a".
◦ Correct: He will return in an hour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "return" — correctly used; it is the base form of the verb, correctly following the modal "will".

• Option 2: "He will" — grammatically correct; a valid subject + modal auxiliary combination.

• Option 3: "hour" — the word itself is spelt correctly; the error lies in the article preceding it, not in the word itself.

NOTE

• Other silent-"h" words that take "an": hour, honest, honour, heir.

• Words beginning with a vowel letter but a consonant sound (and hence take "a"): university, European, one-eyed, useful.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Her sudden arrival has disarranged my plans.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Departure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "arrival" means the act of reaching or coming to a place. (आगमन)
◦ Example: The arrival of the chief guest was delayed by an hour.

• The antonym "Departure" means the act of leaving a place, i.e., the exact opposite of coming/arriving. (प्रस्थान)
◦ Example: Her sudden departure surprised all her colleagues.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Timing: Refers to the point in time at which something happens; it is not an opposite of "arrival".

• Option 2: Entrance: Means the act of entering, or a means of entry (a door/gate) — this is actually close in meaning to "arrival", not its opposite.

• Option 4: Appearance: Means the outward look of a person/thing, or the act of coming into view; not an antonym of "arrival".

NOTE

• Synonyms of "Arrival": Advent, Coming, Appearance.

• Other common antonym pairs of similar words asked by SSC: Entry × Exit, Approach × Retreat, Advance × Retreat.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. It superseded India's previous educational strategy, which was created in 1986.
B. The Indian union cabinet approved the country's national education strategy on 29 July 2020.
C. And it provides a framework for education from the primary grades up to higher education, as well as for vocational training in both urban and rural settings.
D. This policy significantly improves India's educational system. Restructuring India's educational system is the primary goal of the National Education Policy 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. BADC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a para-jumble, identify the introductory sentence — the one that introduces the topic without relying on any earlier reference. Sentence B ("The Indian union cabinet approved the country's national education strategy on 29 July 2020") introduces the subject — the approval of the National Education Policy — and is therefore the opening sentence.

• Sentence A ("It superseded India's previous educational strategy, which was created in 1986") follows B, as the pronoun "It" refers back to the policy approved in B, and it gives background by contrasting it with the earlier 1986 policy.

• Sentence D ("This policy significantly improves India's educational system... National Education Policy 2022") follows A, naming the policy explicitly and stating its overall aim.

• Sentence C ("And it provides a framework for education from the primary grades up to higher education...") logically follows D, continuing with "And" to add a further detail about what the policy does.

◦ Correct sequence: B → A → D → C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: DBCA — incorrect; D cannot open the paragraph as it uses the phrase "This policy", which presumes the policy has already been named.

• Option 2: ABDC — incorrect; A begins with the pronoun "It", which cannot open the paragraph as it has no antecedent yet.

• Option 3: BCDA — incorrect; placing C directly after B breaks the logical link between B (the approval) and A (the comparison with the 1986 policy).

NOTE

• In para-jumbles, always locate the sentence that can stand independently (usually one with a proper noun/subject and no pronoun reference) to identify the opening sentence.

• Words like "It", "This", "And", "As a result" are strong clues to sequencing, since they connect a sentence to the one before it.

question:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.
Mohan __________ the charge of Centre for Life Skills from Mustafa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. took over.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "take over" means to assume control of or responsibility for something, especially from someone else. (कार्यभार संभालना)
◦ Example: Mohan took over the charge of Centre for Life Skills from Mustafa.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "took out" — means to remove something, or to accompany someone somewhere (e.g., "take someone out for dinner"); does not fit the sense of assuming charge.

• Option 2: "took through" — not a standard phrasal verb in this context; "walk/talk someone through" is used to mean explaining a process, not assuming charge.

• Option 3: "took off" — means to remove (clothing), to leave suddenly, or (of an aircraft) to leave the ground; unrelated to assuming responsibility.

NOTE

• Other common phrasal verbs with "take": take up (to start a hobby/job), take after (to resemble a relative), take in (to understand, or to deceive), take on (to accept a challenge/responsibility), take down (to write something, or to remove/dismantle).

question:
Identify the sentence that provides the meaning of the given idiom.
Under the cloud
option_1: The classmates were dancing together under the rain.
option_2: The driver was under suspicion after the police found blood on his car.
option_3: The Red fort looks beautiful amidst the cloudy weather and cold atmosphere.
option_4: It was the best place to sit under the sky with hands full of food.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The driver was under suspicion after the police found blood on his car.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Under a cloud" means to be under suspicion, disfavour, or in a troubled/questionable situation. (शक के घेरे में/संदिग्ध स्थिति में)
◦ Example: The driver was under suspicion after the police found blood on his car — he was under a cloud until the investigation cleared him.

• The correct option must express suspicion or doubt cast upon someone, which only Option 2 conveys.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "The classmates were dancing together under the rain" — describes a literal physical location (under rainfall), not suspicion.

• Option 3: "The Red fort looks beautiful amidst the cloudy weather and cold atmosphere" — refers to literal cloudy weather, not the idiomatic sense of being under suspicion.

• Option 4: "It was the best place to sit under the sky with hands full of food" — describes a pleasant literal scene, unrelated to suspicion or disfavour.

NOTE

• Other idioms with "cloud": "Every cloud has a silver lining" (there is something good in every bad situation), "On cloud nine" (extremely happy), "Cloud someone's judgement" (to impair someone's ability to think clearly).

question:
Choose the option that can substitute the underlined segment correctly and complete the meaning of the sentence.
Bajrang is in extreme pain in his teeth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Agony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Agony" means extreme physical or mental suffering/pain, and is the most precise single word to substitute the phrase "extreme pain". (अत्यधिक पीड़ा)
◦ Example: Bajrang is in agony in his teeth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Ache" means a continuous, usually dull, pain — it does not carry the intensity of "extreme pain" implied in the sentence.

• Option 3: "Hurt" is a general term for pain or injury (physical or emotional) but lacks the sense of extremity/severity.

• Option 4: "Sting" refers to a sharp, brief, localised pain (e.g., from an insect bite or a wound), not sustained extreme pain.

NOTE

• Degree-wise ordering of pain-related words (mild to extreme): Discomfort < Ache < Hurt < Pain < Agony < Anguish.

• Related word: "Excruciating" (adjective) means extremely painful, e.g., "excruciating pain".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Repulcive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Repulsive" — meaning causing strong dislike or disgust, not "Repulcive". (घृणित)
◦ Example: The smell from the garbage dump was absolutely repulsive.

• Spelling key: RE + PULS + IVE — note the letter "s" in the middle (from the root "repulse"), which is missing/replaced by "c" in the misspelt form given.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Nocturnal" — correctly spelt; means active at night or relating to the night.

• Option 3: "Scoreboard" — correctly spelt; a board displaying the score of a game.

• Option 4: "Irrespective" — correctly spelt; means not taking something into account, regardless of.

NOTE

• Other words derived from "repulse" that keep the "s": repulsion, repulsively.

• Commonly confused spelling pairs of this kind (letter substitution errors) tested by SSC: compulsive/complusive, defensive/defencive, expensive/expencive.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'Unsure' from the given sentence.
Himanshi is preparing customised gifts and handicrafts for surprising Mehul on his retirement, but the date is not certain yet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. certain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unsure" means not sure, doubtful, or lacking confidence about something. (अनिश्चित)

• Its antonym is "certain", meaning sure, definite, having no doubt. (निश्चित) — in the given sentence, "the date is not certain yet" shows "certain" as the word whose antonym is "unsure/uncertain".
◦ Example: He was certain of his success, unlike his unsure teammate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "date" — a noun referring to a particular day; not an antonym pair with "unsure".

• Option 3: "customised" — means made or adapted to individual requirements; unrelated in meaning to "unsure/certain".

• Option 4: "handicrafts" — refers to items made by hand; a noun unrelated to the sense of certainty/doubt.

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs of "sure/certain" often tested: Sure × Unsure, Certain × Uncertain, Confident × Doubtful, Definite × Vague.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
He was acquitted of all the charges in the court today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Convicted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "acquitted" means declared not guilty of a criminal charge; formally cleared of an accusation. (दोषमुक्त/बरी करना)
◦ Example: He was acquitted of all the charges in the court today.

• The antonym "Convicted" means declared guilty of a criminal offence after a trial, the exact legal opposite of "acquitted". (दोषी ठहराया गया)
◦ Example: He was convicted of theft and sentenced to two years in prison.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Conformed" means to comply with rules or standards; unrelated to a legal verdict.

• Option 2: "Discharged" means released or let go (e.g., from a duty, hospital, or even a legal case) — this is actually close in meaning to "acquitted", not its opposite.

• Option 3: "Praised" means to express approval or admiration; unrelated to the legal sense of the word.

NOTE

• Legal-vocabulary antonym pairs often tested by SSC: Acquit × Convict, Guilty × Innocent, Plaintiff × Defendant, Prosecution × Defence.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Her modest behaviour was appreciated by everyone in the assembly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. conceited.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "modest" means having or showing a moderate estimate of one's own qualities or achievements; not boastful. (विनम्र)
◦ Example: Her modest behaviour was appreciated by everyone in the assembly.

• The antonym "conceited" means excessively proud of oneself; vain, the exact opposite of being modest. (घमंडी)
◦ Example: His conceited attitude made him unpopular among his colleagues.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "distant" means reserved or aloof in manner, or far away in space/time; not an antonym of "modest".

• Option 2: "unpresuming" is itself a synonym of "modest" (not presuming/not arrogant), and hence cannot be its antonym.

• Option 4: "obvious" means easily perceived or understood; unrelated in meaning to modesty or its opposite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "modest": Humble, Unpretentious, Unassuming, Reserved.

• Other antonym pairs of "modest" tested by SSC: Modesty × Vanity, Humility × Arrogance, Humble × Pompous.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
She looked __________(luminous) in the diamond necklace.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. resplendent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word given in brackets, "luminous", means giving off light; bright or shining. (चमकदार)

• "Resplendent" means attractive and impressive through being richly colourful or sumptuous; shining brilliantly, making it the closest synonym of "luminous" in this context. (शानदार, चमकीला)
◦ Example: She looked resplendent in the diamond necklace.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "impudent" means not showing due respect for another person; disrespectful — unrelated in meaning to "luminous".

• Option 2: "strident" means loud and harsh, usually describing a sound or an aggressively forceful manner; unrelated to brightness.

• Option 3: "transcendent" means going beyond ordinary limits, surpassing the usual; while it can suggest something exceptional, it does not specifically mean "shining/bright" like "resplendent" does.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "luminous": Radiant, Bright, Brilliant, Lustrous, Glowing.

• Words with which "resplendent" is often confused: "Splendid" (magnificent, but not necessarily shining), "Transparent" (see-through).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Once in a blue moon
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Very rare.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Once in a blue moon" means very rarely; almost never. (बहुत कम/कभी-कभार)
◦ Example: He visits his hometown once in a blue moon, as he is settled abroad.

• The phrase draws on the rare astronomical occurrence of a "blue moon" (the second full moon in a single calendar month), which happens only occasionally.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Very ancient" relates to age/antiquity, not frequency; incorrect.

• Option 2: "Very colorful" describes appearance/vividness, unrelated to the idiom's meaning of infrequency.

• Option 4: "Very high" relates to height or degree, not to how often something occurs.

NOTE

• Other idioms of frequency tested by SSC: "Few and far between" (rare, infrequent), "Day in and day out" (every day, continuously), "Now and then" (occasionally).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Who teaches her geography?
option_1: By who geography is taught to her?
option_2: By whom she is taught geography?
option_3: By whom is she taught geography?
option_4: By whom was she taught geography?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. By whom is she taught geography?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Who teaches her geography?" is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Present Tense, with "Who" asking about the subject/doer.

• Rule — Passive voice of a "Who" question in Simple Present Tense:
◦ Active: Who + V1/V5 + Object + Indirect Object?
◦ Passive: By whom + is/am/are + Subject + V3 + Indirect Object?

• Applying the rule: "her" (indirect object) becomes the subject "she"; the auxiliary "is" is used as "she" is singular; the verb "teaches" becomes the past participle "taught"; and "who" becomes "by whom".
◦ Passive: By whom is she taught geography?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "By who geography is taught to her?" is incorrect because it uses "who" instead of the objective form "whom", and the word order after "By who" is wrong for an interrogative passive.

• Option 2: "By whom she is taught geography?" is incorrect because in a question, the auxiliary verb "is" must come before the subject "she" — the correct question order is "is she", not "she is".

• Option 4: "By whom was she taught geography?" is incorrect because "was" is the Simple Past auxiliary, whereas the original sentence is in the Simple Present Tense.

NOTE

• In interrogative sentences beginning with "who" as the object of the action, "who" is converted to "by whom" in the passive, and subject–auxiliary inversion must be maintained.

• "Who" (subjective case) is used as the subject of a verb; "Whom" (objective case) is used as the object of a verb or after a preposition (like "by").

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. Because of the region's scorching heat and aridity, a considerable amount of water evaporates.
B. As a result, the salt and other minerals become increasingly concentrated.
C. It is then unable to exit the lake and is forced to evaporate.
D. The Dead Sea is one of the saltiest bodies of water on the planet, with about ten times the salt content of typical saltwater.
E. This is because water flows into the Dead Sea from a single primary tributary, the Jordan River.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DECAB.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence D ("The Dead Sea is one of the saltiest bodies of water on the planet, with about ten times the salt content of typical saltwater") introduces the topic and is the natural opening sentence.

• Sentence E ("This is because water flows into the Dead Sea from a single primary tributary, the Jordan River") follows D, as "This" refers back to the high salt content mentioned in D and begins to explain its cause.

• Sentence C ("It is then unable to exit the lake and is forced to evaporate") follows E, as "It" refers to the water flowing in from the Jordan River (mentioned in E), continuing the explanation.

• Sentence A ("Because of the region's scorching heat and aridity, a considerable amount of water evaporates") follows C, elaborating on why the water evaporates.

• Sentence B ("As a result, the salt and other minerals become increasingly concentrated") logically concludes the paragraph, as "As a result" signals the final consequence of the evaporation described in A.

◦ Correct sequence: D → E → C → A → B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: DCBAE — incorrect; placing C directly after D breaks the cause-effect link that E establishes (why water is trapped in the lake) before C can logically follow.

• Option 3: DEABC — incorrect; A ("Because of...a considerable amount of water evaporates") cannot immediately follow E, since the sentence needs C first to explain that the inflowing water cannot exit the lake.

• Option 4: DACEB — incorrect; this order breaks the logical flow between E (explaining why water can't exit) and C (which directly continues that idea with "It is then unable to exit").

NOTE

• Look for pronoun/reference chains ("This", "It", "As a result") to establish the correct logical order in a para-jumble.

• "As a result" and "Therefore" type connectors usually appear near the end of a paragraph, signalling a concluding consequence.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A) Bauxite is used as a main raw material for the production of aluminium.
B) Precipitation is a pre-final stage for actual production.
C) Sodium aluminate is acquired in the next step.
D) The smelting process actually extracts aluminium as a final product from its oxide.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ACBD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence A ("Bauxite is used as a main raw material for the production of aluminium") introduces the topic — the raw material used to produce aluminium — and is the natural opening sentence.

• Sentence C ("Sodium aluminate is acquired in the next step") follows A, as it describes the next stage of the process after bauxite is used, signalled by the phrase "the next step".

• Sentence B ("Precipitation is a pre-final stage for actual production") follows C, continuing the sequence of the manufacturing process as the stage before the final one.

• Sentence D ("The smelting process actually extracts aluminium as a final product from its oxide") logically concludes the paragraph, as "actually extracts...as a final product" marks the final step of the process described in B ("pre-final stage").

◦ Correct sequence: A → C → B → D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: ABCD — incorrect; B ("Precipitation is a pre-final stage") cannot directly follow A, since C (acquiring sodium aluminate) is the step that logically comes between bauxite and precipitation.

• Option 3: DCAB — incorrect; D describes the final step of the process (smelting) and therefore cannot be the opening sentence.

• Option 4: ADCB — incorrect; placing D right after A skips the intermediate steps (C and B) entirely, disrupting the step-by-step description of the process.

NOTE

• In process-description para-jumbles, look for sequencing words like "the next step", "pre-final stage", and "final product" to correctly order the stages.

• Aluminium extraction process (for general knowledge): Bauxite → Sodium aluminate → Precipitation (aluminium hydroxide) → Calcination (aluminium oxide/alumina) → Smelting (electrolysis) → Aluminium.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. She dashed from one side to the other, taking care not to destroy the lovely flowers in the garden.
B. Karen took a stroll in a lovely garden full of tulips and butterflies.
C. She discovered a swing constructed of tree branches behind a large bush.
D. Karen went onto the swing without hesitation and began swinging, causing the wind to dishevel her hair.
E. The small girl adored the outdoors and relished the breeze blowing through her hair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. BEACD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence B ("Karen took a stroll in a lovely garden full of tulips and butterflies") introduces the setting and the character, and is therefore the natural opening sentence.

• Sentence E ("The small girl adored the outdoors and relished the breeze blowing through her hair") follows B, elaborating on Karen's feelings during her stroll described in B.

• Sentence A ("She dashed from one side to the other, taking care not to destroy the lovely flowers in the garden") follows E, describing Karen's playful movement in the garden.

• Sentence C ("She discovered a swing constructed of tree branches behind a large bush") follows A, as Karen's movement around the garden (in A) leads to her discovering the swing.

• Sentence D ("Karen went onto the swing without hesitation and began swinging, causing the wind to dishevel her hair") logically concludes the paragraph, describing what Karen does with the swing she discovered in C.

◦ Correct sequence: B → E → A → C → D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: DBCAE — incorrect; D describes Karen swinging on a swing she has not yet been introduced to, so it cannot be the opening sentence.

• Option 3: BDECA — incorrect; placing D (swinging) directly after B (the stroll) is illogical, as Karen has not yet discovered the swing (mentioned in C).

• Option 4: BDCAE — incorrect; again, D (swinging on the swing) is placed before C (discovering the swing), which reverses the logical cause-and-effect order.

NOTE

• In narrative para-jumbles, track the sequence of events/actions performed by the main character (here, Karen) — an action (swinging) cannot precede its cause (discovering the swing).

• Look for the sentence that best sets the scene (introducing character + setting) to identify the opening sentence.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Who broke my glasses?
option_3: By whom were my glasses being broken?
option_4: By whom were my glasses broken?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. By whom were my glasses broken?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Who broke my glasses?" is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Past Tense, with "Who" asking about the subject/doer.

• Rule — Passive voice of a "Who" question in Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Who + V2 + Object?
◦ Passive: By whom + was/were + Subject + V3?

• Applying the rule: the object "my glasses" becomes the subject; it is plural, so the auxiliary is "were"; the verb "broke" becomes the past participle "broken"; and "who" becomes "by whom".
◦ Passive: By whom were my glasses broken?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Who had broken my glasses?" is incorrect because "had broken" is the Past Perfect form, not the Simple Past, and it is also not in the passive voice.

• Option 2: "Who is breaking my glasses?" is incorrect because "is breaking" is the Present Continuous Tense, which changes the meaning and tense of the original sentence, and is not passive.

• Option 3: "By whom were my glasses being broken?" is incorrect because "were being broken" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense ("Who was breaking my glasses?"), not the Simple Past Tense of the original sentence.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the Simple Past passive (was/were + V3) with the Past Continuous passive (was/were being + V3) — the tense of the passive sentence must always match the tense of the original active sentence.

• "Who" (subjective case) becomes "by whom" (objective case after a preposition) when a "who"-question is converted into the passive voice.

question:
Select the correctly spelt option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
Her duel attitude misguides everyone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. dual.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "duel" (a formal fight between two people) is a homophone of "dual", and in the given sentence, the intended meaning requires "dual", meaning consisting of two parts; double or twofold, as in a "dual attitude" (a two-faced/inconsistent attitude). (दोहरा)
◦ Example: Her dual attitude misguides everyone.

• The correct spelling for this intended meaning is "dual", not "duel" (a fight), and certainly not the incorrectly spelt forms "daul" or "deul".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "daul" — an incorrect spelling; not a recognised English word.

• Option 2: "deul" — an incorrect spelling; not a recognised English word.

• Option 4: "dwell" — a correctly spelt English word, but it means "to live in a place" or "to think/speak at length about something"; it is unrelated in both meaning and spelling to the intended word.

NOTE

• Commonly confused homophones tested by SSC: dual/duel, principal/principle, stationary/stationery, complement/compliment, altar/alter.

• "Dual" is often used in compounds like "dual carriageway", "dual citizenship", and "dual personality".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Posters are (1)_________ to promote a brand or pass (2)_________ important information. They can be used for (3)_________ purposes ranging from telling people to be cautious as the floor is wet, to informing them about an upcoming sale or event. They usually include a picture (4)_________ very few words. A suitable (5)_________ makes a poster effective and memorable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. used.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence **"Posters are (1)_________ to promote a brand..." requires the Passive Voice, Simple Present Tense structure: Subject + is/am/are + V3 (past participle)**.

• The verb "use" must therefore appear as its past participle, "used", to correctly complete the passive construction "Posters are used...".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "use" is the base form (V1) of the verb; it cannot follow "are" to form the passive voice.

• Option 2: "uses" is the third-person singular present form of the verb, used in the active voice (e.g., "He uses"); it does not fit the passive structure "are + V3".

• Option 3: "being use" is grammatically faulty — after "being", the past participle "used" is required (i.e., "being used"), not the base form "use".

NOTE

• Passive voice, Simple Present Tense rule: Subject + is/am/are + V3 + (by + agent).

• Common error: students often use the base form instead of the past participle after forms of "be" — always double-check that the verb after "is/am/are/was/were/been/being" is in its V3 (past participle) form.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Posters are (1)_________ to promote a brand or pass (2)_________ important information. They can be used for (3)_________ purposes ranging from telling people to be cautious as the floor is wet, to informing them about an upcoming sale or event. They usually include a picture (4)_________ very few words. A suitable (5)_________ makes a poster effective and memorable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "pass on" means to convey or transmit (information, a message, etc.) to someone else.

• In the sentence **"...or pass (2)_________ important information", the required preposition is "on"**, completing the phrasal verb "pass on" — meaning posters are used to pass on/convey important information.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "away" — "pass away" is a phrasal verb meaning "to die"; it does not fit the intended meaning of conveying information.

• Option 3: "for" — "pass for" means "to be accepted as", which does not fit the sense of transmitting information.

• Option 4: "to" — "pass to" is not an established phrasal verb in standard usage for conveying information in this construction; it does not complete the required idiomatic phrase.

NOTE

• Other common phrasal verbs with "pass": pass out (to lose consciousness, or to graduate from a training institution), pass by (to go past), pass off (to (falsely) present something as something else), pass over (to ignore or disregard someone for a promotion).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Posters are (1)_________ to promote a brand or pass (2)_________ important information. They can be used for (3)_________ purposes ranging from telling people to be cautious as the floor is wet, to informing them about an upcoming sale or event. They usually include a picture (4)_________ very few words. A suitable (5)_________ makes a poster effective and memorable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. varied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence continues, **"They can be used for (3)_________ purposes ranging from telling people to be cautious...to informing them about an upcoming sale or event" — the phrase "ranging from...to..." signals that the purposes described are of different, diverse kinds**.

• "Varied" means showing great diversity; of different kinds, which correctly matches the sense of "ranging from...to..." used in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "little" means "not much" and is used with uncountable nouns to indicate scarcity; it contradicts the sense of "ranging from...to...", which shows diversity, not scarcity.

• Option 3: "much" indicates a large quantity of an uncountable noun, but "purposes" is countable (plural), so "much purposes" is grammatically incorrect, and it does not convey diversity either.

• Option 4: "similar" means "alike, resembling one another", which contradicts the meaning of the sentence, since "ranging from...to..." shows the purposes are different, not similar.

NOTE

• "Much" and "little" are used with uncountable nouns, while "many" and "few" are used with countable nouns — "purposes" being countable and plural rules out both "much" (Option 3) grammatically.

• Words signalling diversity often tested by SSC: varied, diverse, various, assorted, multifarious.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Posters are (1)_________ to promote a brand or pass (2)_________ important information. They can be used for (3)_________ purposes ranging from telling people to be cautious as the floor is wet, to informing them about an upcoming sale or event. They usually include a picture (4)_________ very few words. A suitable (5)_________ makes a poster effective and memorable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. and.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence **"They usually include a picture (4)_________ very few words" requires a simple coordinating conjunction** to join the two elements — "a picture" and "very few words" — that a poster typically includes together.

• "And" is the correct coordinating conjunction here, as it simply adds one item to another without implying contrast, exception, or negation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "nor" is a negative conjunction used to continue a preceding negative (usually paired with "neither"); there is no negation in this sentence, so "nor" cannot be used.

• Option 3: "yet" is a conjunction expressing contrast (meaning "but" or "nevertheless"); there is no contrast between "a picture" and "very few words" in this sentence.

• Option 4: "also" is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, and cannot grammatically join "a picture" and "very few words" within the same clause in this way.

NOTE

• The seven coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS) are: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So — "And" is used for simple addition, "Yet"/"But" for contrast, and "Nor" to continue a negative idea.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Posters are (1)_________ to promote a brand or pass (2)_________ important information. They can be used for (3)_________ purposes ranging from telling people to be cautious as the floor is wet, to informing them about an upcoming sale or event. They usually include a picture (4)_________ very few words. A suitable (5)_________ makes a poster effective and memorable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. caption.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "caption" means a short piece of text accompanying an image or heading, describing or explaining it. (शीर्षक/उपशीर्षक)

• The sentence **"A suitable (5)_________ makes a poster effective and memorable" logically requires a word denoting the descriptive text/heading on a poster, which is exactly what "caption" means.
◦ Example:** A catchy caption can make even a simple poster memorable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "anticipation" (प्रत्याशा): Means the action of anticipating something; expectation. It does not refer to the textual element of a poster.

• Option 3: "quotation" (उद्धरण): Means a group of words taken from a text and repeated by someone else, or a formal statement of the estimated cost of a job; while related to text, it does not specifically mean the descriptive heading of a poster/image.

• Option 4: "caution" (सावधानी): Means care taken to avoid danger or mistakes, or a warning; it does not refer to a poster's descriptive text.

NOTE

• A poster typically has a headline (the main attention-grabbing text), a caption (descriptive text accompanying an image), and a call-to-action (an instruction to the viewer).

• Related word: "Subtitle" — text displayed at the bottom of a screen, translating or transcribing dialogue, is a different but related concept to "caption".
